exams.notes: For standard applicants by examination; for IMLC, must have passed each component of USMLE or COMLEX-USA within three attempts
exams.quote: Passed each component of the United States Medical Licensing Examination (USMLE) or the Comprehensive Osteopathic Medical Licensing Examination (COMLEX-USA) within three attempts

exams.name: State Board of Medical Examiners examination
exams.notes: Required for initial licensure by examination; may be waived for applicants licensed in other states or certified by National Board of Medical Examiners
exams.quote: the board shall, except as herein otherwise provided, examine all qualified applicants for such a license

interval_years.quote: All persons who are licensed to practice medicine and surgery shall be required on or before July 1 biennially to register on the form prescribed by the board and furnished by the executive director of the board, and to pay a biennial registration fee

required.quote: the State Board of Medical Examiners shall require each person licensed as a physician, as a condition for biennial registration pursuant to section 1 of P.L.1971, c.236 (C.45:9-6.1), or as a podiatrist, as a condition for biennial registration pursuant to R.S.45:5-9, to complete a requisite number of credits of continuing medical education

period_years.quote: as a condition for biennial registration pursuant to section 1 of P.L.1971, c.236 (C.45:9-6.1)

value: one credit concerning prescription opioid drugs, responsible prescribing, alternatives to opioids, risks and signs of opioid abuse/addiction/diversion
two credits related to end-of-life care
one credit concerning explicit and implicit bias (for physicians providing perinatal treatment/care to pregnant persons)
topical_requirements.quote: include one credit of educational programs or topics concerning prescription opioid drugs, including responsible prescribing practices, alternatives to opioids for managing and treating pain, and the risks and signs of opioid abuse, addiction, and diversion

available.quote: Any applicant for a license to practice medicine and surgery, upon proving that he has been examined and licensed by the examining and licensing board of another State of the United States or by the National Board of Medical Examiners or by certificates of the National Board of Examiners for Osteopathic Physicians and Surgeons, may, in the discretion of the board of medical examiners of this State, be granted a license to practice medicine and surgery without further examination

requirements.value: Applicant must prove licensure in another state by the respective examining/licensing board or national board, meet all other academic/educational requirements applicable to standard applicants, and pay the license fee. The board has discretion to grant the license without further examination.
requirements.quote: may, in the discretion of the board of medical examiners of this State, be granted a license to practice medicine and surgery without further examination upon payment to the treasurer of the board of a license fee of $150.00; provided, such applicant shall furnish proof that he can fulfill the requirements demanded in the other sections of this article relating to applicants for admission by examination.

D." or "M. B." in connection with his name, or any other title intending to imply or designate him as a practitioner of medicine or surgery in any of its branches

scope_protection.quote: Any person commencing or continuing the practice of medicine and surgery in this State without first having obtained a license, as provided in this chapter or any supplement thereto... shall be liable to a penalty

disciplinary_grounds.description: Obtained a certificate, registration, license or authorization to sit for an examination through fraud, deception, or misrepresentation
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Has obtained a certificate, registration, license or authorization to sit for an examination, as the case may be, through fraud, deception, or misrepresentation

disciplinary_grounds.quote: Has engaged in the use or employment of dishonesty, fraud, deception, misrepresentation, false promise or false pretense

disciplinary_grounds.description: Engaged in gross negligence, gross malpractice or gross incompetence which damaged or endangered the life, health, welfare, safety or property of any person
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Has engaged in gross negligence, gross malpractice or gross incompetence which damaged or endangered the life, health, welfare, safety or property of any person

disciplinary_grounds.description: Engaged in repeated acts of negligence, malpractice or incompetence
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Has engaged in repeated acts of negligence, malpractice or incompetence

disciplinary_grounds.description: Engaged in professional or occupational misconduct as determined by the board
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Has engaged in professional or occupational misconduct as may be determined by the board

disciplinary_grounds.description: Convicted of or engaged in acts constituting any crime or offense with direct or substantial relationship to the regulated activity or inconsistent with public health, safety, or welfare
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Has been convicted of, or engaged in acts constituting, any crime or offense that has a direct or substantial relationship to the activity regulated by the board or is of a nature such that certification, registration or licensure of the person would be inconsistent with the public's health, safety, or welfare

disciplinary_grounds.description: Had authority to engage in the regulated activity revoked or suspended by any other state, agency or authority for reasons consistent with this section
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Has had his authority to engage in the activity regulated by the board revoked or suspended by any other state, agency or authority for reasons consistent with this section

disciplinary_grounds.description: Violated or failed to comply with the provisions of any act or regulation administered by the board
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Has violated or failed to comply with the provisions of any act or regulation administered by the board

disciplinary_grounds.description: Incapable, for medical or any other good cause, of discharging the functions of a licensee in a manner consistent with the public's health, safety and welfare
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Is incapable, for medical or any other good cause, of discharging the functions of a licensee in a manner consistent with the public's health, safety and welfare

disciplinary_grounds.description: Violated any provision of the insurance fraud prevention law or been adjudicated of such a violation
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Has violated any provision of P.L.1983, c.320 (C.17:33A-1 et seq.) or any insurance fraud prevention law or act of another jurisdiction or has been adjudicated, in civil or administrative proceedings, of a violation

disciplinary_grounds.description: Presently engaged in drug or alcohol use likely to impair ability to practice with reasonable skill and safety
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Is presently engaged in drug or alcohol use that is likely to impair the ability to practice the profession or occupation with reasonable skill and safety.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Prescribed or dispensed controlled dangerous substances indiscriminately or without good cause, or where known or should have known substances were to be used for unauthorized consumption or distribution
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Has prescribed or dispensed controlled dangerous substances indiscriminately or without good cause, or where the applicant or holder knew or should have known that the substances were to be used for unauthorized consumption or distribution

disciplinary_grounds.description: Permitted an unlicensed person or entity to perform an act for which a license is required, or aided and abetted an unlicensed person or entity
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Has permitted an unlicensed person or entity to perform an act for which a license or certificate of registration or certification is required by the board, or aided and abetted an unlicensed person or entity in performing such an act

disciplinary_grounds.description: Physician must notify the board within 10 days of any action taken against the physician's license by any other state board or any action affecting privileges, or any pending or final criminal action
disciplinary_grounds.quote: A physician licensed by the State Board of Medical Examiners, or a physician who is an applicant for a license from the State Board of Medical Examiners, shall notify the board within 10 days of: (1) any action taken against the physician's medical license by any other state licensing board or any action affecting the physician's privileges to practice medicine

insurance_required.quote: A physician who maintains a professional medical practice in this State and has responsibility for patient care is required to be covered by medical malpractice liability insurance issued by a carrier authorized to write medical malpractice liability insurance policies in this State, in the sum of $1,000,000 per occurrence and $3,000,000 per policy year

definition_quote.value: the phrase 'the practice of medicine or surgery' and the phrase 'the practice of medicine and surgery' shall include the practice of any branch of medicine and/or surgery, and any method of treatment of human ailment, disease, pain, injury, deformity, mental or physical condition
definition_quote.quote: the phrase "the practice of medicine or surgery" and the phrase "the practice of medicine and surgery" shall include the practice of any branch of medicine and/or surgery, and any method of treatment of human ailment, disease, pain, injury, deformity, mental or physical condition

value: any method of treatment of human ailment, disease, pain, injury, deformity, mental or physical condition
methods_authorized.quote: holds himself out as being able to diagnose, treat, operate or prescribe for any human disease, pain, injury, deformity or physical condition, or who shall either offer or undertake by any means or methods to diagnose, treat, operate or prescribe for any human disease, pain, injury, deformity or physical condition

drug_authority.value: Licensed physicians may prescribe, administer, and dispense drugs and controlled dangerous substances, subject to DEA registration requirements and state limitations on quantities (e.g., Schedule II CDS up to 30-day supply; or multiple prescriptions for up to 90-day supply under specified conditions). Physicians must access the Prescription Monitoring Program before prescribing certain controlled substances.
drug_authority.quote: a physician licensed pursuant to chapter 9 of Title 45 of the Revised Statutes may prescribe a Schedule II controlled dangerous substance for the use of a patient in any quantity which does not exceed a 30-day supply

value: Permit (for practitioners in training / residents / interns)

foreign_medical_graduate_requirements.value: Graduates of foreign medical schools must present a diploma from a legally incorporated professional school or college of a foreign country that was in good standing in the board's opinion, prove four full school years of study, and meet all postgraduate training requirements. For IMLC expedited licensure, the physician must be a graduate of a medical school listed in the International Medical Education Directory or its equivalent.
foreign_medical_graduate_requirements.quote: a diploma from some legally incorporated professional school or college of the United States, Canada or other foreign country, which school or college, in the opinion of the board, was in good standing at the time of the issuance of the diploma

pain_management_education_required.quote: include one credit of educational programs or topics concerning prescription opioid drugs, including responsible prescribing practices, alternatives to opioids for managing and treating pain, and the risks and signs of opioid abuse, addiction, and diversion

opioid_prescribing_limits.value: Initial opioid prescriptions are limited to a 5-day supply under P.L.2017, c.28. Schedule II CDS generally limited to 30-day supply per prescription; multiple prescriptions may be issued for up to 90-day total supply under specified conditions. Schedule II CDS may only be prescribed via telemedicine after an initial in-person examination, with subsequent in-person visits required every three months.
opioid_prescribing_limits.quote: a physician licensed pursuant to chapter 9 of Title 45 of the Revised Statutes may prescribe a Schedule II controlled dangerous substance for the use of a patient in any quantity which does not exceed a 30-day supply

controlled_substance_database_registrati.quote: A practitioner shall register to access prescription monitoring information upon initial application for, or renewal of, the practitioner's CDS registration.

telehealth_prescribing_rules.value: Prescriptions issued via telemedicine are held to the same standard of care as in-person settings. A provider shall not issue a prescription to a patient based solely on responses to an online static questionnaire unless a proper provider-patient relationship has been established. Schedule II CDS may only be prescribed via telemedicine after an initial in-person examination, and a subsequent in-person visit is required every three months for the duration. Exception: stimulant Schedule II CDS for minors under 18 may be prescribed via telemedicine using interactive real-time two-way audio/video if written parental/guardian consent for waiver is obtained.
telehealth_prescribing_rules.quote: The prescription of Schedule II controlled dangerous substances through the use of telemedicine or telehealth shall be authorized only after an initial in-person examination of the patient, as provided by regulation, and a subsequent in-person visit with the patient shall be required every three months for the duration of time that the patient is being prescribed the Schedule II controlled dangerous substance.

telemedicine_license_available.quote: be validly licensed, certified, or registered, pursuant to Title 45 of the Revised Statutes, to provide such services in the State of New Jersey

interstate_medical_licensure_compact_mem.quote: The State of New Jersey enacts and enters into the Interstate Medical Licensure Compact with all other jurisdictions that legally join the compact

physician_assistant_supervision_model.quote: A physician assistant shall be under the supervision of a physician at all times during which the physician assistant is working in an official capacity.

physician_assistant_prescriptive_authori.value: A physician assistant may order, prescribe, dispense, and administer medications and medical devices to the extent delegated by a supervising physician. Controlled dangerous substances (Schedules II-V) may only be ordered or prescribed if the supervising physician has authorized it and the PA has registered with the DEA and complied with all board requirements.
physician_assistant_prescriptive_authori.quote: A physician assistant may order, prescribe, dispense, and administer medications and medical devices and issue written instructions to registered qualifying patients for medical cannabis to the extent delegated by a supervising physician.

malpractice_reporting_required.quote: Notice from an insurer or insurance association or a practitioner, pursuant to section 2 of P.L.1983, c.247 (C.17:30D-17), regarding a medical malpractice claim settlement, judgment or arbitration award or a termination or denial of, or surcharge on, the medical malpractice liability insurance coverage of a practitioner

hospital_privilege_action_reporting_requ.quote: a description of: the revocation or involuntary restriction of privileges at a health care facility for reasons related to the practitioner's competence or misconduct or impairment taken by a health care facility's governing body or any other official of the health care facility after procedural due process has been afforded

impaired_physician_program_authorized.quote: Refer the practitioner to the appropriate licensed health care practitioner treatment program recognized by the State Board of Medical Examiners and promptly notify the medical director of the board of the referral

compelled_mental_physical_exam_authority.quote: the board may order the licensee to submit to medical or diagnostic testing and monitoring, or psychological evaluation, or an assessment of skills to determine whether the licensee can continue to practice with reasonable skill and safety

locum_tenens_permit_available.quote: A lawfully qualified physician or surgeon of another state taking charge temporarily, on written permission of the board, of the practice of a lawfully qualified physician or surgeon of this State during his absence from the State
